name: Ysolde Brennan-Tamboli
description: Ysolde Brennan-Tamboli is considered the founding architect of the 'empathy horror' neural subgenre — productions designed to place audiences inside the emotional experience of systemic suffering without the narrative distance that licensed content typically maintains. Irish-Indian by heritage and raised in Tier 2 Milwaukee, she founded the independent studio Ossian Collective in 2199 and spent six years producing neural-feed works distributed through pirate mesh networks before her 2205 production *Forty Days in the Null Ward* forced an industry reckoning. Her technical mastery of neural-feed architecture is considered equivalent to any Vantablack director, which makes her refusal to license all the more visible.
cultural_impact: Brennan-Tamboli established that neural-feed could function as genuine political testimony rather than entertainment, and her influence is cited by virtually every underground director working in immersive formats.
story_hooks: Brennan-Tamboli is producing a new work and needs access to restricted neural-feed production equipment — equipment that can only be obtained through channels that will attract corporate attention.
A Vantablack talent scout is quietly offering her a fully funded production deal with no content restrictions — and she suspects the offer is a trap designed to get her to sign away her independence.
One of her banned productions contains embedded testimony from someone who has since disappeared, and the family wants to find out if the feed contains information about what happened to them.
